thread:
maria gonzalez: Heads up — finance flagged a billing gap for customer stax-ai. Metering dashboard shows 1,420,312 tokens for Mar 1-7, invoice shows 1,050,298. Filing as P1 with billing team.
kevin park: Oof. Any obvious ingestion errors or replay jobs around that window?
maria gonzalez: Quick glance of event-store shows a 14h consumer lag on ingestion on Mar 3 (offsets ~1250000-1253000). Sending logs.
maria gonzalez: ```
[2026-03-03T04:12:08Z] event-store.consumer: lag=14h, head_offset=1253124, committed=1249800
[2026-03-03T04:14:02Z] metering-service: ack failed for batch 5632, reason=TTL_MISMATCH
```
jordan li: TTL_MISMATCH is weird — we rotated tombstone/retention policy last month (prod retention changed from 90d -> 30d for a specific topic). Could be events dropped by retention before metering consumed them.
sara nguyen: If retention dropped to 30d and some events had older timestamps, the dedupe+ttl rules could have prevented replays from counting them. Anyone know if the replay tool honors the tombstone window?
alice brown: replay-bot should answer that. @replay-bot ?
replay-bot: replay-bot: replay tool obeys event-store tombstone metadata by default (dedupe+ttl=true). It will skip events flagged tombstoned or whose event_time < retention_cutoff unless run with --force-include-tombstones.
kevin park: So if ingestion lag meant metering didn't process before tombstone ran, replaying later would skip them and cause undercount. That matches the gap.
maria gonzalez: Confirmed. I spot-checked offsets 1250105-1250600: lots of customer events for stax-ai that show tombstone=true in raw store but were missing in metering table.
kevin park: Repro steps for ops playbook (short):
1) identify affected offsets: `psql -c "select min(offset), max(offset) from raw_events where customer='stax-ai' and event_time between '2026-03-01' and '2026-03-07'"`
2) check tombstone flags: `select offset, tombstone, event_time from raw_events where offset between X and Y limit 50`
3) run replay with tombstones included: `replay-tool --from-offset X --to-offset Y --dedupe=false --include-tombstones --dry-run` then inspect `metering-audit`
4) when good, run without `--dry-run` on isolated shard and monitor `billing-audit` metric
maria gonzalez: I ran a dry-run for 1250100-1250700 and the replay tool reports ~372k tokens for stax-ai that were previously omitted.
kevin park: Great. Need coordination with finance — we should not change historical invoices until we’re confident.
sara nguyen: I'll schedule a targeted backfill job on dedicated infra to avoid interfering with normal traffic. Plan: start with small chunk (X..Y), validate, then sweep.
alice brown: Finance asked for provisional delta estimate. Maria can you dump the token delta for that window and I'll pass along? Also include a note about which invoices/scope likely affected.
maria gonzalez: Attached quick numbers: `delta_tokens=370,824`, customers_affected=1 (stax-ai), invoices_impacted=Mar-2026-cycle-id-021. Will attach full csv to Jira 7421.

jordan li: One extra precaution: update replay orchestration to default to `--include-tombstones` when running against replay windows overlapping known retention policy change dates. I'll open an infra PR.
kevin park: Follow-ups: 1) run controlled backfill 2) reconcile metering vs invoices and propose credit/adjustment 3) infra PR to change default behavior 4) postmortem about retention rollout communication
maria gonzalez: I'll kick off the controlled backfill in 10m and post status here. Tagging @alice brown for finance sync.
